---
title: "Theming"
subtitle: "Map every visible region of a plot to the `theme()` key that styles it."
engine: markdown
---

A _Gribouille_ plot is a stack of named regions.
Those regions are an outer canvas, an inner panel (or grid of panels), a strip band for facets, a legend column, a title block on top, a caption underneath, and axes around the edges.
Each region is one entry in the [`theme()`](../reference/themes/theme.qmd) dictionary, set with an [`element-text`](../reference/themes/element-text.qmd), [`element-line`](../reference/themes/element-line.qmd), [`element-tick`](../reference/themes/element-tick.qmd), [`element-rect`](../reference/themes/element-rect.qmd), [`element-blank`](../reference/themes/element-blank.qmd), or [`margin`](../reference/themes/margin.qmd) value.
This page is a map.
It shows where each region sits on a real plot, and names the [`theme()`](../reference/themes/theme.qmd) key that controls it.
It also links worked examples for the common overrides.

The diagram below is a real plot.

## Region to theme key reference

The table below names every region the renderer styles and the [`theme()`](../reference/themes/theme.qmd) key that controls it.
Each axis family cascades in three steps: per-side (`-x-bottom`, `-x-top`, `-y-left`, `-y-right`) falls back to per-axis (`-x`, `-y`), which falls back to the unprefixed family.
Setting `axis-text` alone styles all four sides at once.
The panel grid cascades by weight then axis: per-axis (`-x`, `-y`) falls back to the weight (`panel-grid-major`, `panel-grid-minor`), which falls back to `panel-grid`.
Minor gridlines default to half the major weight in the same colour, and a blank `panel-grid` blanks both weights.

| Region                                                                                       | Key(s)                                                                                                                            | Element type                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Outer plot rectangle.                                                                        | `plot-background`.                                                                                                                | [`element-rect`](../reference/themes/element-rect.qmd).                                                         |
| Breathing room around content (painted rect grows outward to wrap it).                       | `inset` on `plot-background` and `legend-background`. Ignored on `panel-background`, `strip-background`, `legend-bar`.            | [`margin`](../reference/themes/margin.qmd).                                                                     |
| Outer whitespace reservation.                                                                | `outset` on `plot-background`, `panel-background`, `legend-background`, `legend-bar`. Ignored on `strip-background`.              | [`margin`](../reference/themes/margin.qmd).                                                                     |
| Title, subtitle, caption.                                                                    | `plot-title`, `plot-subtitle`, `plot-caption`.                                                                                    | [`element-text`](../reference/themes/element-text.qmd).                                                         |
| Drawing area inside a facet.                                                                 | `panel-background`.                                                                                                               | [`element-rect`](../reference/themes/element-rect.qmd).                                                         |
| Gridlines inside the panel, by weight and axis.                                             | `panel-grid`, `panel-grid-major`, `panel-grid-minor`, `panel-grid-major-x`, `panel-grid-major-y`, `panel-grid-minor-x`, `panel-grid-minor-y`. | [`element-line`](../reference/themes/element-line.qmd).                                                         |
| Facet header band.                                                                           | `strip-background`, `strip-text`.                                                                                                 | [`element-rect`](../reference/themes/element-rect.qmd), [`element-text`](../reference/themes/element-text.qmd). |
| Axis line, per side.                                                                         | `axis-line`, `axis-line-x`, `axis-line-y`, `axis-line-x-bottom`, `axis-line-x-top`, `axis-line-y-left`, `axis-line-y-right`.      | [`element-line`](../reference/themes/element-line.qmd).                                                         |
| Axis ticks (stroke, colour, and length), per side.                                           | `axis-ticks`, `axis-ticks-x`, `axis-ticks-y`, `axis-ticks-x-bottom`, `axis-ticks-x-top`, `axis-ticks-y-left`, `axis-ticks-y-right`. | [`element-tick`](../reference/themes/element-tick.qmd).                                                         |
| Minor tick marks (log sub-decade ticks), per axis.                                           | `axis-ticks-minor`, `axis-ticks-minor-x`, `axis-ticks-minor-y`.                                                                   | [`element-tick`](../reference/themes/element-tick.qmd).                                                         |
| Axis tick labels, per side.                                                                  | `axis-text`, `axis-text-x`, `axis-text-y`, `axis-text-x-bottom`, `axis-text-x-top`, `axis-text-y-left`, `axis-text-y-right`.      | [`element-text`](../reference/themes/element-text.qmd).                                                         |
| Axis title, per side.                                                                        | `axis-title`, `axis-title-x`, `axis-title-y`, `axis-title-x-bottom`, `axis-title-x-top`, `axis-title-y-left`, `axis-title-y-right`. | [`element-text`](../reference/themes/element-text.qmd).                                                         |
| Discrete legend box.                                                                         | `legend-background`, `legend-title`, `legend-text`.                                                                               | [`element-rect`](../reference/themes/element-rect.qmd), [`element-text`](../reference/themes/element-text.qmd). |
| Continuous colour bar (chrome reuses `legend-background` / `legend-title` / `legend-text`).  | `legend-bar`, `legend-ticks`.                                                                                                     | [`element-rect`](../reference/themes/element-rect.qmd), [`element-line`](../reference/themes/element-line.qmd). |
| Shared cascade parents (fields inherit down to every descendant surface unset on the child). | `text`, `line`, `rect`.                                                                                                           | Element constructors.                                                                                           |
| Base colour roles (drive geom colour resolution and theme mixing).                           | `ink`, `paper`, `accent`.                                                                                                         | Colour.                                                                                                         |
| Layer aesthetic defaults.                                                                    | `geom`.                                                                                                                           | [`element-geom`](../reference/themes/element-geom.qmd).                                                         |

You can hide any key with [`element-blank`](../reference/themes/element-blank.qmd) in place of its normal element.
That is how [`theme-minimal`](../reference/themes/theme-minimal.qmd) drops the axis line, the panel background, and the tick marks, for example.
A blank surface also reserves no space, so blanking `axis-ticks` reclaims the tick depth.
Blanking `axis-text` on one side, such as `axis-text-y-right`, hides that side's tick labels and the width they would have taken.

## Inheritance cascade

Every styled surface walks a parent chain root-to-leaf at render time.
The most specific record wins; unset fields inherit from the parent.
Two patterns repeat: base records (`text`, `line`, `rect`) feed every descendant surface, and each axis family fans out by axis then by side.

Text sizes accept either an absolute length or a ratio.
A ratio such as `80%` scales the parent surface size.
Setting the base `text` size therefore rescales every surface that inherits via a ratio (axis titles, tick labels, legend text, and so on).
An absolute length such as `12pt` pins that surface outright and ignores the cascade.

```{typst}

//| label: fig-theme-cascade-base
//| fig-cap: "Base records feed every descendant. Setting `text`, `line`, or `rect` cascades to every surface in its column; fields unset on the child inherit from the parent."
//| output-filename: "theme-cascade-base.svg"
//| file: _theme-cascade-base.typ
//| alt: "Three columns of trees. Each base record (text, line, rect) sits on the left of its column, with edges fanning out to every descendant surface stacked vertically on the right: text feeds axis-text, axis-title, legend-text, legend-title, strip-text, plot-title, plot-subtitle, plot-caption; line feeds panel-grid, axis-line, axis-ticks, legend-ticks; rect feeds panel-background, plot-background, strip-background, legend-background, legend-bar."
```

```{typst}
//| echo: false
//| label: fig-theme-cascade-axis
//| fig-cap: "Axis family cascade (one template, four families). Replace `<family>` with `axis-line`, `axis-ticks`, `axis-text`, or `axis-title`. Per-side leaves cascade up to per-axis, then to the family root. `axis-ticks-minor` hangs off `axis-ticks` with a per-axis variant of its own."
//| output-filename: "theme-cascade-axis.svg"

//| alt: "Tree diagram of the axis family cascade. A single root node labelled <family> splits into <family>-x and <family>-y, each of which then splits into two per-side leaves: <family>-x-bottom and <family>-x-top under the x branch, <family>-y-left and <family>-y-right under the y branch."
```

## Override one region

The lightest possible change is to pass a single record into [`theme()`](../reference/themes/theme.qmd) for the region you care about.
The example below lifts the [`axis-title`](../reference/themes/element-text.qmd) and [`axis-text`](../reference/themes/element-text.qmd) sizes, paints the [`panel-background`](../reference/themes/element-rect.qmd) cream, and softens the [`panel-grid`](../reference/themes/element-line.qmd).
Every other surface keeps its default.

```{typst}
//| echo: true
//| output-filename: "theming-override.svg"
//| alt: "Scatter plot with cream panel background, soft gridlines, and enlarged axis titles."
#let df = range(0, 12).map(i => (x: i, y: i * i * 0.1))

#plot(
  data: df,
  mapping: aes(x: "x", y: "y"),
  layers: (
    geom-line(stroke: 1.2pt, colour: rgb("#d6604d")),
    geom-point(size: 3pt, fill: rgb("#d6604d")),
  ),
  theme: theme(
    axis-title: element-text(size: 12pt),
    axis-text: element-text(size: 10pt),
    panel-background: element-rect(fill: rgb("#f7f0e7")),
    panel-grid: element-line(colour: rgb("#d9cfbf")),
  ),
  labels: labels(
    title: "theme() overrides",
    subtitle: "Larger axis titles, a cream panel fill, and a soft grid",
    x: "Step",
    y: "y = 0.1 × x²",
  ),
  width: 12cm,
  height: 7cm,
)
```

Each line maps directly to one row in the [region table](#region-to-theme-key-reference): change a single key, the matching region updates, nothing else moves.

## Ticks and their labels

Tick marks are one record: [`element-tick`](../reference/themes/element-tick.qmd) carries the mark's `colour`, `stroke`, and `length` together, on `axis-ticks` and its per-axis, per-side, and minor variants.
A `length` given as a ratio scales the length inherited from the parent surface, exactly as `size` and `stroke` do elsewhere.
The y ticks below therefore come out half the length of the x ticks, without naming an absolute value.

```{typst}
//| echo: true
//| output-filename: "theming-ticks.svg"
//| alt: "Scatter plot with long tick marks on the x axis, half-length ticks on the y axis, and no tick labels on the right-hand side."
#let df = range(0, 12).map(i => (x: i, y: i * i * 0.1))

#plot(
  data: df,
  mapping: aes(x: "x", y: "y"),
  layers: (geom-point(size: 3pt, fill: rgb("#d6604d")),),
  scales: scales(y: scale-continuous(secondary: dup-axis())),
  theme: theme(
    axis-line: element-line(stroke: 0.5pt),
    axis-ticks: element-tick(length: 0.25cm, stroke: 0.8pt),
    axis-ticks-y: element-tick(length: 50%),
    axis-text-y-right: element-blank(),
  ),
  labels: labels(x: "Step", y: "y = 0.1 × x²"),
  width: 12cm,
  height: 7cm,
)
```

Tick labels live entirely in `axis-text`, so hiding them is the same per-side [`element-blank`](../reference/themes/element-blank.qmd) as anywhere else.
The duplicated right-hand axis above keeps its marks and drops its labels, along with the width they would have reserved.
Blanking `axis-ticks` on a side does the same for the marks.
Minor marks inherit that record through `axis-ticks-minor`, and default to half the major length in the same stroke.
Those are the sub-decade ticks that [`guide-axis-logticks`](../reference/guides/guide-axis-logticks.qmd) adds on a log axis.

## Tune the outer canvas

Grow the outer plot rectangle past its content with [`element-rect`](../reference/themes/element-rect.qmd)'s `inset` field (inner padding).
Reserve whitespace around the rectangle with the `outset` field (outer margin).
Each takes a [`margin`](../reference/themes/margin.qmd) with any subset of `top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left`; sides left at `auto` add nothing.

```{typst}
//| echo: true
//| output-filename: "theming-margin.svg"
//| alt: "Two stacked scatter plots; the lower one has a tinted plot-background grown via element-rect inset on every side."
#let accent = rgb("#1f77b4")
#let d = range(0, 10).map(i => (x: i, y: i * 0.5))

#let panel(title, theme-arg) = plot(
  data: d,
  mapping: aes(x: "x", y: "y"),
  layers: (
    geom-line(stroke: 1pt, colour: accent),
    geom-point(size: 2pt, fill: accent),
  ),
  labels: labels(title: title, x: "X", y: "Y"),
  theme: theme-arg,
  width: 12cm,
  height: 6cm,
)

#grid(
  columns: 1,
  row-gutter: 0.4cm,
  panel("Default plot-background", theme-minimal()),
  panel(
    "plot-background: element-rect(inset: margin(top: 0.6cm, right: 0.6cm, bottom: 0.9cm, left: 1.6cm))",
    theme-minimal(plot-background: element-rect(
      fill: rgb("#f7f0e7"),
      inset: margin(
        top: 0.6cm,
        right: 0.6cm,
        bottom: 0.9cm,
        left: 1.6cm,
      ),
    )),
  ),
)
```

`inset` grows the painted rectangle outward to wrap its content; only `plot-background` and `legend-background` honour it.
`outset` reserves outer whitespace.
On `panel-background`, `legend-background`, and `legend-bar`, the reservation widens the surrounding cetz chrome slot and shrinks the panel canvas.
On `plot-background`, `outset` wraps the rendered block in `pad()`.
`strip-background` ignores both fields: the facet band has no surrounding slot to grow or reserve into.
Facet column and row gutters come from `panel-spacing`, which defaults to `0.5cm`.
Set a length to space both axes equally, or a `(x:, y:)` dictionary to space them independently.
A per-facet `facet-wrap(gutter:)` or `facet-grid(gutter:)` overrides the theme.
`axis-title.margin` controls the gap between tick labels and the axis title.
Gaps around any other text surface use the per-element `margin` field on its [`element-text`](../reference/themes/element-text.qmd).

## Complete vs partial themes

[`theme()`](../reference/themes/theme.qmd) is the full base: it populates every surface listed in the [reference table](#region-to-theme-key-reference).
Use it when you want to start from scratch and define each region yourself.

The library ships eight curated overrides on top of that base.
Each one is a thin function that returns a theme with a handful of fields replaced.
Everything else cascades from [`theme()`](../reference/themes/theme.qmd).

| Function                                                    | Effect                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`theme-minimal`](../reference/themes/theme-minimal.qmd).   | Drops the axis line, the panel background, and the tick marks. The library default. |
| [`theme-bw`](../reference/themes/theme-bw.qmd).             | Black-and-white frame, white panel, light grid.                                     |
| [`theme-classic`](../reference/themes/theme-classic.qmd).   | Axis lines only, no grid, no panel background.                                      |
| [`theme-grey`](../reference/themes/theme-grey.qmd).         | Grey panel background with a white grid.                                            |
| [`theme-light`](../reference/themes/theme-light.qmd).       | Light frame and grid on a white panel.                                              |
| [`theme-dark`](../reference/themes/theme-dark.qmd).         | Dark frame and grid on a dark panel.                                                |
| [`theme-linedraw`](../reference/themes/theme-linedraw.qmd). | Black frame, dark grid, white panel.                                                |
| [`theme-void`](../reference/themes/theme-void.qmd).         | Everything removable removed; useful for inset thumbnails.                          |

The `theme-sub-*` helpers go one level finer: they bundle the keys that move together for a single region.
For example, [`theme-sub-axis`](../reference/themes/theme-sub-axis.qmd) accepts `line`, `ticks`, `text`, `title`, and rewrites the four corresponding [`theme()`](../reference/themes/theme.qmd) keys for you.
The full set is [`theme-sub-axis`](../reference/themes/theme-sub-axis.qmd), [`theme-sub-axis-x`](../reference/themes/theme-sub-axis-x.qmd), [`theme-sub-axis-y`](../reference/themes/theme-sub-axis-y.qmd), [`theme-sub-axis-bottom`](../reference/themes/theme-sub-axis-bottom.qmd), [`theme-sub-axis-top`](../reference/themes/theme-sub-axis-top.qmd), [`theme-sub-axis-left`](../reference/themes/theme-sub-axis-left.qmd), [`theme-sub-axis-right`](../reference/themes/theme-sub-axis-right.qmd), [`theme-sub-legend`](../reference/themes/theme-sub-legend.qmd), [`theme-sub-panel`](../reference/themes/theme-sub-panel.qmd), [`theme-sub-plot`](../reference/themes/theme-sub-plot.qmd), and [`theme-sub-strip`](../reference/themes/theme-sub-strip.qmd).

Finally, [`theme-set`](../reference/themes/theme-set.qmd) installs a theme as the document-wide default so subsequent `plot()` calls pick it up without an explicit `theme:` argument.
